messages.subject: [statnet_help] one ergm for multiple networks
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

is it possible to use the ergm-package for a simultaneous analysis of 
multiple networks (in my case: of same size and same content)? I know 
that this can be done in PNet and Stocnet-SIENA with the help of 
'structural zeros', i.e., by creating a joint adjacency matrix of all 
networks' nodes and differentiating between "unconnected" and 
"unreachable by design". But PNet and Stocnet-SIENA both require 
interactive clicking through Windows menus, and I'd prefer to do this in 
R, so a solution in the ergm-package would be preferable. Is there one?

Greetings,
Christian


PS - I realise that related questions have been asked before - without 
getting an answer - by Vic Louisier, or Moses Boudourides.


--

messages.subject: [statnet_help] one ergm for multiple networks
messages.body_plain:
hi christian,

i had a related earlier question on this too, and so can pass along the advice i received from steve and pavel. i'll caution, however, that while this indeed provided me with a solution for my problem that makes intuitive sense to me (and seems to directly parallel the "structural zeroes" situation in Siena), there may be other reasons for which this fix is undesirable/inappropriate, especially for the case of multiple networks? so i will still be curious to hear if others have further thoughts.

basically you can do exactly what you suggest- create a joint adjacency matrix of all networks- and then i'm aware of two possible ways to prohibit ties "between" networks:

1) more straightforward: create a node attribute that has a different value for membership in each of the different networks; include a "nodemix" term in your model, and use the "base" argument to only include those effects from the mixing matrix that correspond to ties ACROSS networks; and fix those parameters at -Inf (i have had mixed experience with this in the past... sometimes you may not have to fix the parameter because ergm will recognize that no ties are present and do this for you automatically... sometimes it does not and so you have to do this manually using offset, see below).

2) more cumbersome: basically the same thing, but do this using an edge covariate instead of a node covariate. in other words, create a matrix where values for ALL ties WITHIN networks are set to zero, and ALL ties ACROSS networks are set to one, feed this into your model using an edgecov term, and again fix that effect at -Inf using the offset() function, e.g. offset(edgecov(X)).

i hope this is helpful... but others please let us know if for some reason this approach is problematic! or if there is an easier approach i'm unaware of. best wishes,

-kevin

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Problem specifying theta0 in simulate.ergm
messages.body_plain:
Hello, Ben,

In case this is still of use, one thing you could try is replacing

simulate.ergm(mod,theta0=z)->new

with

simulate.ergm(mod,theta0=z,burnin=10000)->new

One thing that might be happening is that the burn-in is too short to
zero out all of the within-grade ties.

                             I hope this helps,
                             Pavel

> I am trying to simulate networks based on a ERG model with certain

> mod$coef->z
> z[2:7]<- -50 #change all the nodematch grade coefs

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Isolates in ergm
messages.body_plain:
Dear Wincent,

The isolates are a part of the information you have about the social
structure, so they most certainly should be kept in the network. (In
principle, if you excluded the isolates, you would have to fit a model
conditional on having no isolates.)

                I hope this helps,
                Pavel

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Isolates in ergm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Wincent,

To follow on with that: I agree with Pavel - you would rarely want to 
exclude isolates, and if you did, it should be because you believe that 
they are somehow excluded from the stochastic process you are modeling; 
I have a hard time coming up with a reasonable example, but if you were 
in that case, you would then need to condition your model on no isolates.

Now, assuming you do include the isolates in the network for estimation 
-- whether you then want to explicitly include an isolates term in the 
model or not, or consider some other set of model parameters that would 
address the preponderance of isolates (other degree terms, for instance) 
is really a question of the hypotheses that you are interested in 
testing.  This is a substantive question that only you and your 
collaborators can really answer.

Cheers,
Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Criteria for ergm convergence?
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I'd have a question regarding the convergence of ergms. Specifically, I
have a directed network of 113 nodes, and have found a model that seems to
fit quite well (according to the idegree,odegree, esp, and triadic census
GoF plots). However, the log-likelihood keeps on increasing, even if I do,
say, 500 iterations (with MCMC samplesize 100k). Does this mean that my
model is not well specified, or should I just run more iterations?

Also, why is the improvement of log-likelihood limited to 20 in each
iterations? Is that a setting we could override?

I'm attaching the log and the GoF plot. Any help would be appreciated.

Thanks, and happy holidays!
Balazs

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Criteria for ergm convergence?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Balazs,

I am working on alternative methods to estimate ERGM.

A problem for the default method in ergm package (Hunter and Handcock,
2006) is that
the approximation used for simulated maximum likelihood may still be very
poor.

This implies that iterating may not give a convergent algorithm.

I suggest you to try with the "Stepping" method based on Hummel et al., 2011.

It is already implemented in ergm package (check the R help of
control.ergm).

I think that it is a great improvement also if it can still suffer in
presence near degeneracy and stability problems.

Marry Xmas to everybody.

Nicola



> Dear All,
>
> I'd have a question regarding the convergence of ergms. Specifically, I
have a directed network of 113 nodes, and have found a model that seems
to
> fit quite well (according to the idegree,odegree, esp, and triadic
census
> GoF plots). However, the log-likelihood keeps on increasing, even if I
do,
> say, 500 iterations (with MCMC samplesize 100k). Does this mean that my
model is not well specified, or should I just run more iterations?
>
> Also, why is the improvement of log-likelihood limited to 20 in each
iterations? Is that a setting we could override?
>
> I'm attaching the log and the GoF plot. Any help would be appreciated.
>
> Thanks, and happy holidays!
> Balazs
>


-- 
Soriani Nicola
Scuola di Dottorato in Scienze Statistiche XXIII Ciclo
Dipartimento di Scienze Statistiche, Universit? di Padova
Stanza 122 - Tel. 049 827 4174
Ph.D. Student
Department of Statistical Sciences
University of Padova, Italy
